title: Contains Duplicate
statement: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return false if every element is distinct.
hints: Sorting the array puts identical items next to each other in O(n log n).
A Set stores unique elements in O(1) average lookup.

solutions.title: Sort & Scan Neighbor
solutions.complexity: Time: O(n log n) | Space: O(1)

solutions.title: Hash Set Early Exit

editorial.approach: Brute-force pairwise checking takes O(n^2) time, and sorting takes O(n log n). The optimal approach uses a hash set: scan the array element by element, checking if the current element is already present in the set. If found, return true immediately; otherwise insert it into the set.
editorial.why_optimal: Average-case O(1) set lookups yield O(n) time and O(n) space, allowing early termination on the very first duplicate encountered.
editorial.pitfalls: In languages without proper hashing on negative integers or composite objects, using array lookups instead of true hash tables leading to accidental quadratic degradation.
